verses.text: At daybreak, all the chief priests and elders of the people met and planned to put Jesus to death.
They tied him up, led him away, and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the governor.
When Judas, who had betrayed Jesus, saw that he had been condemned, he felt remorse. He brought the thirty silver coins back to the chief priests and elders
and said, “I sinned by betraying an innocent man.” They replied, “That’s your problem. Deal with it yourself.”
Judas threw the silver into the temple, left, and went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests picked up the coins and said, “We can’t put this in the treasury; it’s blood money.”
After discussing it, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
That is why the field is still called the Field of Blood.
Then what the prophet Jeremiah had spoken came true: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price set for him by the people of Israel,
“and used them to buy the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
Jesus stood before the governor, who asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You’re saying it.”
When the chief priests and elders accused him, he gave no answer.
Pilate asked him, “Don’t you hear all the charges they’re bringing against you?”
But Jesus didn’t answer even one charge, and the governor was greatly amazed.
At the festival, the governor had a custom of releasing one prisoner chosen by the crowd.
At that time they had a well-known prisoner named Barabbas.
So when the crowd gathered, Pilate asked, “Who do you want me to release: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
He knew they had handed Jesus over because they were jealous of him.
While Pilate was sitting on the judge’s seat, his wife sent him a message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man. I suffered badly in a dream about him today.”
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and have Jesus destroyed.
The governor asked them, “Which of the two should I release?” They said, “Barabbas!”
Pilate asked, “Then what should I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?” They all shouted, “Crucify him!”
He asked, “Why? What crime has he committed?” But they shouted even louder, “Crucify him!”
When Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and a riot was starting, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. “I’m innocent of this man’s blood,” he said. “You’re responsible.”
All the people answered, “Let his blood be on us and on our children!”
Then Pilate released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus whipped and handed him over to be crucified.
The governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s headquarters and gathered the whole company around him.
They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him.
They twisted thorn branches into a crown and placed it on his head. They put a stick in his right hand, knelt in front of him, and mocked him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spat on him, took the stick, and struck him on the head with it.
After mocking him, they took off the robe, put his own clothes back on him, and led him away to crucify him.
As they were leaving, they met a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.”
They offered Jesus sour wine mixed with gall. He tasted it but wouldn’t drink it.
After they crucified him, they divided his clothes by casting lots.
Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.
Above his head they posted the charge against him: “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
Two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
People passing by insulted him and shook their heads.
They said, “You said you could tear down the temple and rebuild it in three days. Save yourself! If you’re God’s Son, come down from the cross!”
The chief priests also mocked him, along with the scribes, Pharisees, and elders.
“He saved others, but he can’t save himself! If he’s Israel’s King, let him come down from the cross now, and we’ll believe him.
“He trusts God, so let God rescue him now if he wants him. He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
Even the robbers crucified beside him insulted him in the same way.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
About three, Jesus cried out loudly, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” That means, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
Some people standing there heard him and said, “He’s calling Elijah.”
At once, one of them ran, took a sponge, soaked it in sour wine, put it on a stick, and offered it to him to drink.
The others said, “Leave him alone. Let’s see if Elijah comes to save him.”
Jesus cried out loudly again and released his spirit.
At that moment, the temple curtain split in two from top to bottom. The ground shook, and rocks split apart.
Tombs opened, and many bodies of the holy people who had died were raised to life.
After Jesus was raised, they came out of the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many people.
When the centurion and those guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and everything that happened, they were terrified and said, “This really was God’s Son!”
Many women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and cared for him were there, watching from a distance.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He was also a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a large stone across the tomb’s entrance and left.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting across from the tomb.
The next day, after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees went together to Pilate
and said, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was alive, he said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’

“So order the tomb to be guarded until the third day. Otherwise his disciples might come, steal him, and tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’ Then this last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate told them, “You have guards. Go and secure it as best you can.”
So they went and made the tomb secure. They sealed the stone and stationed guards there.
